newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Drivers still holding cargo 'hostage' in Colombiao.
newsitem.headline: Drivers still holding cargo 'hostage' in Colombiao.

text.p: About 120 truck drivers continued to hold "hostage" tonnes of cargo in Colombia's main Pacific coast port Monday, the bulk of it coffee ready for shipment abroad.
The truckers are demanding hundreds of thousands of dollars in "standby" payments for time lost during the nine-day dockworkers' strike that paralyzed the port of Buenaventura until last Friday.

Jose Rios, regional head of the overland cargo transporters association, said about 2,000 tonnes of cargo, 90 percent of it coffee, was affected by the truckers' job action and their refusal to let their cargo be off-loaded and placed onto awaiting ships.

National Coffee Exporters' Association said in a statement issued late Friday that Jorge Javier Sanchez, chief representative of the National Coffee Growers' Federation in Buenaventura, had been appointed to negotiate a speedy end to the truckers' sitdown strike.
But Rios said the negotiations had led nowhere by midday Monday. Sanchez could not be reached for immediate comment.
Unless coffee affected by the strike is freed up soon, exporters face the likelihood of breaking December contracts and delivering late on January shipments.
